title: the model is told what the run has done, and the transcript is a projection of the journal and not a second copy of the run
intent: The live run of the wave 41 on the code of the wave 46 (2026-11-17, 16:15 and 16:26) made 108 and 122 calls of tools and changed nothing in the repository: the model read `AGENTS.md' again and again, read the plan and the claim of the wave 46 twice, measured a race with experiments of its own in `/tmp', and every answer of the model was a plan ('I'll start by reading the repository rules').  The reason is in the harness and not in the model: every request of the harness starts a fresh conversation with the model.  `yeah-turn--ask' hands the transport a prompt, and the prompt is all the model is told — the messages that came before, the calls the model made, the results it got and its own answers are nowhere in the request, so the model cannot continue the work and begins the task over.  The machinery of the context exists and is not on the road to the model: `yeah-context-project' and `yeah-session-project' compute a projection, the compaction and the pruning write their events into the journal, and the projection itself never reaches a request.  The wave gives the model the transcript of the run: a projection of the journal, the tail of the records of the run, put together when the model is asked and put in front of the prompt.  The transcript names the call the model made, the result it got and the answer it gave, and it ends with the words that keep the work where it is ('Do not start the work over: continue from here.').  The first request of a run carries the request as it is: a run that has done nothing has nothing to tell.  The transcript is a projection and not a second copy of the run: the journal keeps the plain message it was written with, and the projection is put together on the way to the model.  The wave was found by two live runs and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of those runs with a fake transport: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness.
objection: The transcript is a string in the prompt, so the cost of every request of a run grows with the work of the run: the projection is cut at twelve records of the run, and the result of a tool is cut at six hundred characters, so a run of a hundred calls pays for the tail of its own work in every request.  A long run therefore pays for the same work again and again, and the provider is charged for it.  The projection of the context (`lib/yeah-context.el') is the machinery that is meant to answer this, and it is still not on the road to the model: the compaction and the pruning write their events into the journal, but the summary of the work is not what the model is told, and the transcript of the wave is a plain tail of the records.  The wave does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md): the model is now told what it has done, but a model that keeps announcing its next step is still a model that does not act.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order, and the runs that found this defect were the runs of the wave 41.
refuted_by: a request that follows the work of the run carries no trace of the work: neither the call the model made, nor the result it got, nor the answer it gave; or the journal holds the transcript of the run, so that the journal keeps a second copy of the run
note: Both controls of the wave were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made the check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `the-model-is-told-what-the-run-has-done' takes the transcript out of the request, and the check fails on four assertions: the second request does not carry the transcript of the run, and it names neither the call the model made, nor the result of the call, nor the answer the model gave.  The control of `the-transcript-is-a-projection-and-not-a-second-copy-of-the-run' writes the transcript into the journal, and the check fails on one assertion: the journal holds the transcript, so the projection is a copy of the run.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right, and both times it was wrong in a way that hid the defect it was written for.  The first version collected the failures with the polarity reversed: `yeah-check--fail' reports a failure when its argument is nil, and the second and third checks handed it the negation of the condition they wanted, so the check reported a failure exactly when the condition held — the check failed on a harness that worked and would have passed on a harness that was broken.  The second version recorded the prompts of the model into the parameter of the fake transport and not into the variable of the caller, so the check saw an empty list of prompts and could not tell a harness that asks the model from a harness that does not.  The two defects of the check were found by reading the check and not by the check: the mechanism of the wave was shown to work by a direct reading of the prompts in an Emacs that printed them, and the check was then read against that reading.  A check that cannot fail is a comment, and a check that fails when the harness is right is worse: it is a comment that reads as a proof.  The wave also changed the code of the unit test of the control (`tests/unit/test-yeah-control.el'), because the prompt of a request now carries the transcript and the test looked for the prompt itself; the test now looks for the prompt by its tail, which is the part the harness does not change.  The wave broke a check of the repository and the map of the method caught it: the check of the control of the wire (`tests/checks/check-wire-control.el') drives a server whose fake model answers the prompt `again' and only that prompt, and it compared the prompt with `(equal prompt "again")' -- an exact comparison, which the transcript makes false.  The prompt of the last request of that session therefore never completed, and the check failed on its own assertion.  The fix was in the check and not in the harness: the fake model now matches the prompt by its tail, which is the part the harness does not change.  A wave that changes the shape of the prompt breaks every check that matched the prompt exactly, and the check has to be rewritten: the prompt of a request is not a constant, and the part of it that the harness owns is the tail.
